data.content_ref: inline:Contradiction via a structural counterexample: SRC_005's cycle-based obstructions (monochromatic 2-factor cycles matched by opposite colors) contradict SRC_002's implicit assumption that the ONLY obstructions are sparse matching cuts counted by a Poisson heuristic. Each 3-regular graph has exponentially many 2-factors, giving exp(Θ(n)) candidate frozen configurations — a combinatorial obstruction source SRC_004's Θ(1) expectation never accounts for. If even a polynomially small fraction of these are reachable, the constant 1−q of SRC_002 is REFUTED, and the limit is 0. It is REFUTED IF cycle-based frozen configurations are dynamically unreachable from uniform random starts (SRC_005's own countercondition), in which case SRC_002's constant survives against this attack.
